rows.claim: The prereg froze every pass/fail bar before any arm ran and banned moving bars, rerolling, rescue interpretations, and bar-shopping once results exist; a failed bar files as FAIL/DISPUTED with numbers.
rows.quote: Bars below are frozen BEFORE any arm runs. No bar moves after results exist. A failed bar files as FAIL/DISPUTED with numbers; no rescue interpretations, no rerolls, no bar-shopping.
rows.steal: Freeze numeric pass/fail bars in the filed spec BEFORE the first run of any replication, rerun, or workflow wave (GAUNTLET W4 rerun bars, mickey17 fold thresholds); a failed bar files with numbers, never gets reinterpreted to pass.
rows.falsifier: Any receipt where a bar value changed after results existed, or a FAIL row filed with a rescue interpretation instead of numbers.

rows.claim: Amendment 1 recalibrated the Arm C bar in the only legal window: after Arm B's budget curve existed but before Arm A or Arm C produced any row, naming the measured calibration error (bar demanded a rate no judge meets at 50 states).
rows.quote: This amendment is filed AFTER Arm B (their system, our hardware) but BEFORE Arm A and Arm C produce any row.
rows.steal: Treat prereg amendments as legal only between a completed prior arm and any data from the affected arm; the amendment must cite the measured reason for the change, and everything else in the original prereg stands unchanged.
rows.falsifier: An amendment whose arm already had data when it was filed, or an amendment with no measured reason attached.

rows.law: adversarial review kills your own bad arm before it fires
rows.claim: The Grok 4.7 adversarial pass ruled Arm C's substitution inference UNSOUND before launch: at budget 200 the stack's own search already solves 30/30 with and without merge, so a >=15/30 line cannot separate the judge from saturated search; the verdict retired the arm and is itself testimony.
rows.quote: the decision that would license “gemma substitutes the trained judge” is a >=15/30 line at a budget where this stack's own search already solves 30/30 with and without merge, installed after that curve was known.
rows.steal: Before firing a claim-bearing arm, adversarially review whether its pass bar can be cleared by a confound (merge, width, saturation); a UNSOUND verdict retires the arm permanently (this lane did not rerun it), and the prescribed fix is a null arm at fixed 0.5 scores plus a substitution sentence allowed only when gemma strictly beats the null.
rows.falsifier: A substitution claim filed from a cleared bar while a null arm (every score fixed 0.5, same loop, both budgets) matches the arm's solve count.

rows.claim: Arm B (vendored Apache-2.0 code, shipped judge, zero LLM, seed-11 problems) reproduced the published numbers exactly on local hardware at both budgets, PASSing the frozen >=27/30 bar and licensing the mechanism steal.
rows.quote: At budget 200: one-line 70% (21/30, matches their published 21/30 exactly), frontier-no-merge 100%, interference 100% (30/30, matches published exactly). ARM B VERDICT: PASS at the frozen >=27/30 bar.
rows.steal: Reproduce the source's headline number exactly on your own hardware at the same seed before stealing mechanisms; an exact match converts a paper claim into a stealable mechanism (merge-on-identical-state for mickey17 folds, trained-judge shape for the estate judge-lane).
rows.falsifier: A vendored rerun missing the published number at the same seed with no named hardware/env delta; the miss then files as the finding and the steal is off.
